text.p: Following are some major events to have occurred on August 24 in history.
79 - The cities of Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae were destroyed and thousands of people killed by an eruption of Mount Vesuvius in Italy.
410 - Alaric and his Visigoth army sacked Rome.
1516 - Ottoman Sultan Selim I defeated the Mameluke army near Aleppo, securing Syria for the empire.
1572 - The St Bartholomew's Day Massacre in France brought the death of up to 70,000 Protestant Huguenots.

1680 - Colonel Thomas Blood, Irish adventurer who stole the Crown Jewels from the Tower of London in 1671, died. Captured after the theft, he insisted on seeing the king, Charles II, who pardoned him.
1759 - William Wilberforce born. English statesman, philanthropist and reformer, instrumental in the abolition of the slave trade in the British West Indies in 1807.
1772 - William I of Orange, King of the Netherlands 1815-40, was born.
1814 - British forces captured Washington DC and burned down many landmarks. President James Madison fled.
1865 - Ferdinand I, King of Romania, born. Although a believer in German strength, he was responsible for his country joining the allies in World War One.
1893 - A fire in the south of Chicago left 5,000 homeless.
1898 - Russian Tsar Nicholas II proposed a conference of major powers for the "preservation of general peace by disarmament".
1899 - Jorge Luis Borges born. Argentine author, regarded as one of Latin America's most influential writers.
1905 - Siaka P. Stevens born. Became the first executive president of Sierra Leone in 1971. He created a one-party state and remained in power until his retirement in November 1985.
1921 - The Battle of Sakarya River began between Greece and Turkey. After three weeks of fighting the Turks were victorious.
1922 - Arab states meeting at Nablus rejected the British mandate for Palestine given by the League of Nations.
1953 - The British colonial government of Kenya broadcast a call to Mau Mau nationalist guerrilla fighters to surrender.
1954 - U.S. President Dwight Eisenhower signed into law the Communist Control Act, outlawing the Communist Party.
1954 - Getulio Vargas, president of Brazil 1930-45 and 1951-54, committed suicide.
1958 - Johannes Strijdom (or Strydom), South African prime minister since 1954, died in office.
1965 - Saudi Arabia and Egypt signed a ceasefire deal for Yemen. They had been backing rival sides in the Yemeni civil war.
1968 - France became the fifth nuclear power when it exploded a hydrogen bomb near Fugataufa Atoll, midway between Australia and South America.
1975 - Death sentences on former Greek prime minister Georgios Papadopoulos and two other leaders of the 1967 coup were commuted to life imprisonment.
1989 - Poland became the first Soviet-bloc country since the late 1940s to appoint a non-communist prime minister, Tadeusz Mazowiecki.
1990 - A Reno, Nevada, judge ruled that the British heavy metal rock band Judas Priest was not responsible for the deaths of two youths who shot themselves after listening to the band's music.
1990 - Irish hostage Brian Keenan was freed by his Islamic Dawn Organisation captors in west Beirut after 52 months in captivity.
1991 - The Ukraine parliament declared independence from Moscow, subject to confirmation by a referendum in December.

1994 - Israel and the PLO initialled an accord giving autonomy to Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank in five important areas of life -- education, health, taxation, social welfare and tourism.
1995 - China expelled U.S. human rights activist Harry Wu Hongda, just hours after he was sentenced to 15 years in jail for spying.

1995 - Life magazine photographer Alfred Eisenstaedt died. His photograph of a sailor kissing a nurse in New York's Times Square became one of the best known images of America's joy at Japan's surrender in World War Two.
